title: Organic Compound Families Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A library sorts books by subject, a school sorts students by age, and chemists sort millions of carbon compounds into families. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we learn the classification of organic compounds.

On the molecule bench, the family tree grows one question at a time: acyclic (aliphatic) chains, alicyclic rings like cyclohexane, aromatic benzenoid and non-benzenoid compounds, and heterocyclic rings like tetrahydrofuran, furan and pyridine. Then functional groups (-OH, -CHO, -COOH), the homologous series link by link (each member one CH2, 14 u, bigger), and ethane vs ethanol side by side. A worked example on the alkane family, the exam trap, an original JEE / NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 80 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three sorting jobs
0:34 Why sort organic compounds
1:02 The family tree: acyclic, alicyclic, aromatic, heterocyclic
2:02 Functional groups: -OH, -CHO, -COOH
2:27 Homologous series, link by link
3:06 Ethane vs ethanol: what makes the difference
3:44 Worked example: the alkane family
4:26 Exam trap: is every ring aromatic?
4:54 Practice question (JEE / NEET pattern)
5:29 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: IUPAC Nomenclature of Organic Compounds. Why is this molecule called 2-methylpentane?
